lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Complex Solutions, Polynomials, and the Binomial Theorem
lessonRef.focus: the fundamental theorem of algebra and counting roots
lessonRef.title: Reteach and varied practice: the fundamental theorem of algebra and counting roots

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: These two examples show the same idea in two different formats.

items.prompt: Is the product of two rational expressions rational?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Factor x² + 49 completely over the complex numbers.
choices: (x + 7i)²

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 2. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 5, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 2, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 1, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^4, find the coefficient of the term x^1·y^3.
Complete the statement: the sum of two rational expressions …
choices: is always a rational expression, because numerators and denominators multiply directly
need not be a rational expression, because the denominators may differ
is always a rational expression, because a common denominator can always be formed
is always a rational expression, because dividing is multiplying by the reciprocal

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Factor x² + 36 completely over the complex numbers.
choices: (x + 6i)²

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 3. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 6, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 4, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 2, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^4, find the coefficient of the term x^3·y^1.
Complete the statement: the quotient of two rational expressions, where the divisor is not the zero expression …
choices: is always a rational expression, because a common denominator can always be formed
is always a rational expression, because numerators and denominators multiply directly
need not be a rational expression, because the denominators may differ
is always a rational expression, because dividing is multiplying by the reciprocal

items.prompt: Factor x² + 4 completely over the complex numbers.
choices: (x + 2i)²
